steps: Rinse the soaked matki and pressure cook it with water just to cover for 1 whistle on medium; keep the cooking water.
Chop the onion and tomato finely and crush the ginger and garlic.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium, let the mustard seeds pop, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing for a few seconds.
Fry the onion on medium for 3 to 4 minutes until soft and pink, then add the ginger and garlic for a minute.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala and cook on medium-low for about 5 minutes, until oil shows at the edges.
Add the matki with a splash of its water, the salt and jaggery, cover and simmer on low for 4 to 5 minutes, until the beans are tender.
Scatter over the coriander leaves and serve hot with roti or bhakri.
note: After the 8-hour soak the matki needs about a day more wrapped in a damp cloth to sprout, so start two days ahead. Garam masala stands in for goda masala, which one source also allows; this is the semi-dry usal, not the thin misal curry.
